 CORAM:HONOURABLE MR. JUSTICE M. R. MENGDEY
Date : 06/11/2025  ORAL ORDER 1.

The Applicants have filed this Application under Section 483 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 for enlarging the Applicants on Regular Bail in connection with FIR being C.R.
No.11822023240803 of 2024 registered with Maroli Police Station, Navsari for the offence punishable under Sections 420, 467, 468, 471, 120(B) of the Indian Penal Code.
2.
Heard learned advocate Ms. Mittal N. Patel appearing for the applicants.

She submitted that the applicants have been arrested in connection with the present offence on 29.06.2024 and since then,
they are in custody.
The applicants have undergone incarceration for a period of more than one year.
The trial of the offence is not likely to conclude in the near future.

The applicants had earlier preferred Criminal Miscellaneous Application No.18987 of 2024 which was allowed to be withdrawn by this Court on 01.10.2024 and liberty was granted in favour of the applicants to file an application after a period of NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/19993/2025 ORDER DATED: 06/11/2025 undefined 9 months if the trial did not get over within the said period.

The trial of the offence is not Umeshbhai Balubhai Patel vs State Of Gujarat on 6 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/183785509/
1 yet over.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: She therefore submitted to allow the present application and enlarge the applicants on bail subject to suitable conditions.

3. Learned APP has opposed the application contending that after the withdrawal of earlier application filed by the applicants, there is no change in circumstances and therefore, the present successive application for bail is not maintainable.
She therefore submitted to dismiss the application.
4. Heard learned advocates for the parties.

The applicants had earlier preferred Criminal Miscellaneous Application No.18987 of 2024 which was allowed to be withdrawn by this Court on 01.10.2024 since this Court was not inclined to exercise its discretion in favour of the applicants.
However, this Court had granted liberty to the applicants to file a fresh application after a period of 9 months if the trial did not get over in the interregnum.
This Court vide order dated 06.10.2025 had called for the report from the concerned Trial Court as regards the status of trial.

The report of the Trail Court 17.10.2025 indicates that, out of 36 witnesses cited by the prosecution in the charge sheet, 19 witnesses were already examined on the date on which the report was submitted.
The APP has drawn the attention of this Court to the fact that after the date of the report of the concerned Court, several other witnesses have also been examined.
Thus, the trial of the offence is in progress and majority of the witnesses have already been examined.
NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/19993/2025 ORDER DATED: 06/11/2025 undefined 5.
Having with regard to these facts, this Court is not inclined to exercise discretion in favour of the applicants at this stage.
Hence, the application is dismissed.

(M. R. MENGDEY,J) AHS Umeshbhai Balubhai Patel vs State Of Gujarat on 6 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/183785509/
